text:
Devon: Heads up — we started seeing GPU provisioning backlogs in ap-south1 ~10m ago after the KVM jump-host fleet rollout. Nodes are stuck at 'awaiting-console'.
Maya: saw the alert, looking now. is this regional or global?
Samir: ap-south1 first, small spike in eu-west1 tailing. other regions healthy so far.
Alex: any recent BMC/firmware changes on the jump hosts? we pushed that bmc bridge fw last night right?
Devon: yes, last night we rolled v2.1.4 for the out-of-band jump host appliances (managed BMC proxy). correlative timeline lines up.
Maya: logs from the jump hosts show connection handles not closing. suspecting a conn leak between kvm-proxy -> jump-host -> bmc.
Samir: paste from one affected host:
```
# ss -tn state time-wait sport = :5900 | wc -l
23456
# netstat -anp | grep TIME_WAIT | grep 5900 | head
TCP 10.0.4.2:5900 10.0.4.10:54023 TIME_WAIT -
...lots of TIME_WAIT...
```
Maya: who owns kvm-proxy? looks like ephemeral port exhaustion on the jump-hosts, new sessions can't be created so console handoff hangs.
Alex: kvm-proxy team is me/Kei. quick check: kube pods for provisioning queue show many pending due to node readiness probe failing (console timeout).
Devon: kubectl excerpt: `pods/worker-provision-*-ap-south1   0/1   Pending   0     2m` with annotated event: `console handshake timeout`.
Kei: workaround idea: rotate jump-host pods (kill one at a time) to clear TIME_WAIT backlog + bump net.ipv4_tcp_max_tw_buckets and tcp_tw_reuse on the hosts. will that break anything?
Samir: we can do rolling restart of kvm-proxy pods in ap-south1, should be safe. But if BMC fw is causing sockets to not properly close, restarts could re-expose after traffic resumes.
Maya: ops-bot created incident INC-2026-893 with priority P2. tagging security to double-check secure-boot toggles (we don't want nodes to reboot into non-attested state while we fiddle with BMC).
Devon: good call — after the fw push some machines also flipped secureboot attr on the BMC side for a subset. That explains intermittent failures for those hosts where console negotiation expects signed port.
Alex: action list: (1) Roll kvm-proxy pods in ap-south1 (Kei). (2) Temporarily increase tcp_tw_reuse/time_wait settings (Samir). (3) Revert the BMC bridge fw on one canary rack if restarts don't help (Devon). (4) Run a small prov batch to validate.
Kei: starting rolling restart now, 1 pod every 30s with readiness check. will call when first one is back. :spinner:
Maya: also patching the provisioning controller to extend console handshake timeout by +20s to reduce retries while we stabilize.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-893 created by Maya. Severity: P2. Channels: #eng-infra, #incidents.
Kei: first restart complete — observed TIME_WAIT drop from 23k -> 3k on that host, provisioning backfill for a handful of pods succeeded.
Devon: great. confirm if secureboot flip persisted on any node after restart?
Samir: checked 10 nodes — 2 still reporting bmc.attr.secureboot=enabled but console fails on one. looks like a firmware state machine race where attribute toggles mid-handshake.
Alex: for the canary revert, what's the easiest path? revert package on the BMC gateway via the jump-host OTA manager?
Devon: yes. I'll revert kube daemonset image for the BMC bridge on rack r-ap-south1-12 and monitor. will do during the next low-traffic window unless we need immediate rollback.
Maya: cost note — provisioning delays are queuing GPU requests and pushing up preemptible spin-ups in other regions; estimate ~$1.6k extra per hour if unresolved for >1h. Ops lead signed off on fast remediation.
Kei: rolling restarts finished across ap-south1. aggregate TIME_WAIT normalized, provisioning backlog cleared ~80%.
Samir: applied sysctl tweaks to host kernel (tcp_tw_recycle off, tcp_tw_reuse=1, net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range widened). watching for side effects.
Devon: after revert on the canary rack (r-ap-south1-12) secureboot attr remained stable and console handshakes completed for 6/6 nodes. looks like fw v2.1.4 introduced the race.
Maya: creating follow-up ticket to halt remainder of the bmc bridge rollout until patch available and add extra e2e prov test covering secureboot toggles.
Alex: please attach the netstat/ss dumps and the pod event logs to the incident. we need clear RCA notes.
Devon: attaching logs to INC-2026-893. summary: BMC bridge v2.1.4 introduced connection teardown race leading to ephemeral port exhaustion on jump hosts, causing console handshakes to hang and GPU node provisioning delays; mitigations: kvm-proxy rolling restart, sysctl tuning, canary FW revert.
Maya: thanks team. postmortem scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Kei: I'll put a temporary alert rule for TIME_WAIT >10k on jump-hosts so we catch earlier. :thumbsup:
Samir: leaving watch on metrics for 2h, will escalate if it creeps back up.
Alex: nice work. Keep incident open until revert planned fleet-wide or patched build out.
Maya: closing thread here but updates will go to INC-2026-893.
